title: Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove the United States Armed Forces from hostilities against the Islamic Republic of Iran.
official_title: Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove the United States Armed Forces from hostilities against the Islamic Republic of Iran.
summary: This concurrent resolution invokes the War Powers Resolution to direct the President to end U.S. military hostilities against Iran within 30 days unless Congress explicitly authorizes them through a declaration of war or a specific authorization for the use of military force. It states that U.S. forces were introduced into hostilities against Iran on February 28, 2026, and includes carve-outs preserving self-defense, a defensive troop presence, and intelligence-sharing. It expresses the will of both chambers and does not change any law.
brief: Directs the President, under section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove U.S. Armed Forces from hostilities against Iran within 30 days of February 28, 2026, absent congressional authorization.

top_lines.headline: War Powers Directive on Iran
subs: Directs the President to end hostilities against Iran within 30 days
Triggered by U.S. forces entering hostilities against Iran on February 28, 2026
Exception only if authorized by a declaration of war or specific military-force authorization

top_lines.headline: Carve-Outs Preserved
subs: Does not bar self-defense of U.S. forces, facilities, or allies from imminent attack
Does not bar a defensive troop presence in the region
Does not disrupt intelligence collection, analysis, or coalition intelligence-sharing

likelihoodReason: The concurrent resolution failed in the House on May 14, 2026 on a 212-212 tie vote (a tie defeats the measure). Because it did not pass the House, it cannot proceed to the Senate, and the matter is effectively closed for this measure.

items.main: States congressional findings, including that U.S. Armed Forces were introduced into hostilities against Iran on February 28, 2026, and that Congress has not declared war or provided specific statutory authorization for those hostilities.
items.detail: The findings describe Iran as the leading state sponsor of terrorism and an adversary of the United States, cite its ballistic missile program, terrorist proxies, and pursuit of a nuclear weapon, and note Congress's sole constitutional power to declare war under Article I, Section 8. They also state the President is required to brief Congress on the deployment of forces, including the estimated scope and duration of their use, under the War Powers Resolution.

sections.label: Section 2 — Termination of Use of Force

items.main: Directs the President, under section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove U.S. Armed Forces from hostilities against Iran no later than 30 days after February 28, 2026, unless explicitly authorized by Congress.
items.detail: The termination covers hostilities against Iran or any part of its government or military, including potential ground forces in a combat role or used for occupation. A rule of construction states the section does not prevent the U.S. from defending itself, its forces, diplomatic facilities, or allied states from imminent attack; does not prevent maintaining a troop presence in the region for defensive purposes; and does not force removal of forces in the region not engaged in hostilities against Iran.

sections.label: Section 3 — Rule of Construction Relating to Intelligence Sharing

items.main: Provides that nothing in the resolution may be construed to influence or disrupt intelligence, counterintelligence, or investigative activities relating to threats in or emanating from Iran or surrounding countries.
items.detail: Covers the collection of intelligence, the analysis of intelligence, and the sharing of intelligence between the United States and any coalition partner where the President determines such sharing is appropriate and in the national security interests of the United States.

sections.label: Section 4 — Rule of Construction Relating to Nonauthorization of the Use of Military Force

items.main: States that, consistent with section 8(a)(1) of the War Powers Resolution (50 U.S.C. 1547(a)(1)), nothing in the resolution may be construed as authorizing the use of military force.
items.detail: Rule of construction — clarifies the resolution does not itself authorize force.

gaps: The resolution directs removal from hostilities against Iran but does not define what constitutes the 'hostilities' that began on February 28, 2026.
The resolution preserves a defensive troop presence and self-defense but does not specify who determines whether a given action is offensive hostilities or permitted self-defense.
The resolution sets a 30-day removal deadline but does not address enforcement if the President does not comply.
